entries.name: NeuroPath
entries.introduction: Nine cognitive games connect four laboratories: Memory, Attention, Logic and Flexibility. Choose a focused puzzle or build a varied training routine.
entries.purpose: Offer structured cognitive engagement through associative recall, visual selection, flexible classification and deliberate reasoning. The activities are designed for practice and curiosity, not diagnosis or treatment.
entries.audience: Independent readers who enjoy visual, memory and reasoning challenges.
entries.age_guidance: Choose by reading comfort and puzzle familiarity. A numeric age recommendation has not yet been published.
entries.difficulty: Automatic is the default. Per-game Easy, Medium and Hard choices are available, with custom options for supported experiences.
entries.status: In development. Application mechanics are documented here; this is not a playable web game.
objectives: Explore different ways of remembering, attending and reasoning.
Choose a comfortable challenge and revisit instructions without rushing.
Review personal in-app performance rather than interpret results as an IQ or health score.
offers: Memory Lab brings together word associations, ordered light events and change detection.
Attention Lab combines target selection with careful orbital planning.
Logic Lab contains the signature NeuroWeave and CodeQuest experiences.
Flexibility Lab explores changing classifications and hidden transformations.

interaction.see: Four laboratories and their nine games, with game descriptions, difficulty choices and three clearly marked signature experiences.
interaction.hear: Optional interaction tones and ambient sound. No speech recording pack is supplied.
interaction.do: Open a laboratory, review a game and select guided practice or a difficulty before playing in the application.
interaction.feedback: Completed play records genuine activity-specific measures such as accuracy, moves or sequence recall. These are app performance indicators, not medical assessments.
interaction.progression: Automatic difficulty responds to comparable recent results. Manual choices remain in control; separate daily plans offer 5, 10, 15, 20 or 30 minute estimated routines.
interaction.help: Open How to Play for contextual instructions and guided practice. Pause when needed; use the application Back or Home action to leave through its save flow. Completed attempts offer replay and analysis.

entries.name: Memory Lab
entries.introduction: Build a mental link between a real Spanish word and a familiar meaning, then retrieve that association in two different ways.
entries.purpose: Exercise associative encoding, typed recall and recognition using a small set of real words.
entries.audience: Independent readers who enjoy visual, memory and reasoning challenges.
entries.age_guidance: Choose by reading comfort and puzzle familiarity. A numeric age recommendation has not yet been published.
entries.difficulty: Easy: 3 word pairs. Medium: 5. Hard: 7–9. Automatic selects a level from comparable recent performance.
entries.status: In development. Application mechanics are documented here; this is not a playable web game.
objectives: Form a memorable word–meaning association.
Recall the word without seeing the original pair.
Recognize its meaning among shuffled alternatives.
offers: A visible study stage before recall begins.
Typed Spanish-word recall followed by meaning recognition.
A curated vocabulary with meanings in the selected interface language.

interaction.see: A small set of Spanish words paired with familiar meanings; later, a meaning prompt or shuffled recognition choices.
interaction.hear: Pronunciation recordings have not been supplied. Optional touch effects and ambience do not replace spoken words.
interaction.do: Study the pairs, choose Ready, type the Spanish word for each meaning, then choose meanings during recognition.
interaction.feedback: Answers are compared with the actual word or meaning. Correct answers and errors are recorded across the two response stages.
interaction.progression: Larger pair sets increase the amount to remember. Recall and recognition are distinct stages of the same game.
interaction.help: Create a mental image linking each word to its meaning. Open How to Play or guided practice; pause and save before leaving when needed.

tutorial.title: Study the pairs
tutorial.text: Look at each Spanish word and its meaning. Build an association that makes the pair memorable.

tutorial.title: Hide the study display
tutorial.text: Choose Ready when you want to begin recall. The original pairs are hidden.

tutorial.title: Recall the word
tutorial.text: Read the meaning prompt, type its Spanish word and submit one answer at a time.

tutorial.title: Recognize the meaning
tutorial.text: Next, choose the matching meaning for each word from the shuffled options.

tutorial.title: Review or replay
tutorial.text: Complete the remaining items and review the recorded outcome. Use replay, help or return to Memory Lab.

entries.name: Light Paths 2.0
entries.introduction: Follow a sequence of numbered neural lights, then reconstruct the events in the displayed direction. Advanced rounds add colors, pulse durations and distracting signals.
entries.purpose: Explore ordered visual recall while keeping the required direction and enabled signal attributes in mind.
entries.audience: Independent readers who enjoy visual, memory and reasoning challenges.
entries.age_guidance: Choose by reading comfort and puzzle familiarity. A numeric age recommendation has not yet been published.
entries.difficulty: Six tiers use 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 or 24 nodes. Initial sequence ranges are 3–4, 5–7, 4–7, 5–8, 6–10 and 8–12 events. Automatic and manual/custom settings are available.
entries.status: In development. Application mechanics are documented here; this is not a playable web game.
objectives: Recall a sequence forward or in reverse.
Remember enabled color and short/long pulse information.
Separate solid numbered signals from marked distractions.
offers: Forward, Reverse and Mixed directions, shown before the sequence.
Four named colors with shape cues and explicit Short/Long controls.
Correction without advancing past a wrong answer, plus hints, retry, undo and skip.
Ten interactive tutorial lessons introducing each layer of the task.

interaction.see: A numbered neural network, a clear direction cue and solid lit nodes. Higher tiers may add color, pulse duration, layout changes between rounds and hollow × distractions.
interaction.hear: Optional game effects and haptics. Sound is not required to reproduce the visible sequence; no narration pack is supplied.
interaction.do: Watch the sequence without tapping. During recall, choose enabled color/pulse information and the next node in the indicated order. Measured presses are an optional alternative to explicit Short/Long controls.
interaction.feedback: A wrong response leaves the same sequence position open for correction. Results distinguish first responses, corrections, assistance and skipped rounds.
interaction.progression: Automatic mode reviews multiple rounds and changes demands gradually. Manual settings remain in control. A soft daily target and configurable free-play round count do not interrupt an active round.
interaction.help: Use Next hint, Watch this round again, Undo last response or Skip round. Help use is recorded as assistance. Save and return to Memory Lab preserves progress.

tutorial.title: Read the direction
tutorial.text: Check whether this round asks for Forward, Reverse or a direction within Mixed practice.

tutorial.title: Watch the sequence
tutorial.text: Choose Show sequence and observe the solid numbered lights. Ignore hollow × lights, edge lights and traveling sparks.

tutorial.title: Remember whole events
tutorial.text: When enabled, notice each event’s node, color and short or long pulse. The same attributes stay with the event when recall is reversed.

tutorial.title: Reproduce the events
tutorial.text: Wait for recall to open. Choose color and pulse controls when shown, then select each remembered node in the indicated direction.

tutorial.title: Correct or ask for help
tutorial.text: A mismatch keeps the current position. Try again or use a hint, replay, undo or skip; those forms of assistance are recorded.

tutorial.title: Continue or save
tutorial.text: At a round boundary choose another round or finish. Use Save and return to Memory Lab if leaving before completion.

entries.name: EchoShift
entries.introduction: Study a sequence of events, hold their details in mind, then decide which events have changed.
entries.purpose: Practice comparing a remembered event with a later version while separating its shape, color and number.
entries.audience: Independent readers who enjoy visual, memory and reasoning challenges.
entries.age_guidance: Choose by reading comfort and puzzle familiarity. A numeric age recommendation has not yet been published.
entries.difficulty: Easy: 3 events. Medium: 5. Hard: 7. A short hidden interval separates study and recall.
entries.status: In development. Application mechanics are documented here; this is not a playable web game.
objectives: Encode more than one attribute of an event.
Retain the event at its numbered position.
Judge change using what was actually shown.
offers: Original events with shape, color and numeric value.
A hidden interval rather than an answer visible beside the question.
Changed and Unchanged responses for each corresponding event.

interaction.see: Numbered events during study, followed by their later versions after a hidden interval.
interaction.hear: Optional touch effects and ambience; the task is visual and does not require recorded speech.
interaction.do: Study each event, choose Ready, then decide whether any of its attributes changed.
interaction.feedback: Each judgment is compared with the original event and recorded before the next event appears.
interaction.progression: Higher levels increase the event set from 3 to 5 to 7.
interaction.help: Compare one attribute at a time. How to Play and guided practice explain the sequence; pause/save controls are available.

tutorial.title: Study each position
tutorial.text: Notice the shape, color and number belonging to each numbered event.

tutorial.title: Start the recall interval
tutorial.text: Choose Ready; the original display is hidden for a short interval.

tutorial.title: Compare from memory
tutorial.text: Inspect the later event at the corresponding position and decide Changed or Unchanged.

tutorial.title: Complete the set
tutorial.text: Judge each event separately, then review the outcome or return to Memory Lab.

entries.name: Target Hunt
entries.introduction: Find every symbol that matches the displayed target rule while leaving distractors unselected.
entries.purpose: Practice deliberate visual selection using the attributes that matter for the current task.
entries.audience: Independent readers who enjoy visual, memory and reasoning challenges.
entries.age_guidance: Choose by reading comfort and puzzle familiarity. A numeric age recommendation has not yet been published.
entries.difficulty: Easy: 9 symbols with a shape rule. Medium: 16 symbols with a color rule. Hard: 25 or 36 symbols with both attributes.
entries.status: In development. Application mechanics are documented here; this is not a playable web game.
objectives: Read a target rule before responding.
Scan a display systematically.
Check every selected symbol against the requested attributes.
offers: Shape, color and combined target rules.
Randomized symbol positions with genuine matching targets.
Found-target marking and recorded selection errors.

interaction.see: A target rule above a grid of differently shaped and colored symbols.
interaction.hear: Optional interaction tones and ambience; no audio-only target instructions are claimed.
interaction.do: Scan the grid and tap every symbol matching the stated rule.
interaction.feedback: Correct targets remain marked; wrong selections count as errors. A previously selected cell cannot be counted again.
interaction.progression: More symbols and combined attributes increase visual demands. The round ends when every target is found.
interaction.help: Scan one row at a time and check only the requested attributes. How to Play, guided practice and pause are available.

tutorial.title: Read the rule
tutorial.text: Check whether this round asks for a shape, a color or both.

tutorial.title: Scan steadily
tutorial.text: Work across the grid in a consistent order and compare each symbol with the rule.

tutorial.title: Select matches
tutorial.text: Tap matching symbols and leave distractors alone. Found targets remain marked.

tutorial.title: Finish the search
tutorial.text: Continue until every matching target is found, then review the recorded selections.

entries.name: OrbitMind
entries.introduction: Rotate orbital rings and exchange aligned tokens until each token reaches its specified ring and position.
entries.purpose: Practice keeping track of spatial goals while planning a sequence of controlled moves.
entries.audience: Independent readers who enjoy visual, memory and reasoning challenges.
entries.age_guidance: Choose by reading comfort and puzzle familiarity. A numeric age recommendation has not yet been published.
entries.difficulty: Easy: 2 rings. Medium: 3. Hard: 4. Each ring has six slots, and generated puzzles require an exchange as well as rotations.
entries.status: In development. Application mechanics are documented here; this is not a playable web game.
objectives: Track both token identity and position.
Plan alignment before making an exchange.
Compare the resulting arrangement with the whole goal.
offers: One-step left and right ring rotations.
Exchanges between neighboring rings only when their slots align.
Move counting and a clear target arrangement.

interaction.see: Orbital rings, distinguishable tokens and target ring/slot information.
interaction.hear: Optional interaction effects and ambience; no spoken spatial directions are supplied.
interaction.do: Rotate rings to align adjacent tokens, exchange them, and rotate toward their target slots.
interaction.feedback: Every valid move changes the actual arrangement and increments the move count. Completion requires all token identities and slots to match.
interaction.progression: Additional rings create more relationships to coordinate. The moves are reversible and generated boards are checked for solvability.
interaction.help: Align slots before exchanging tokens, then check the token’s required ring and slot. Use written help, guided practice or pause.

tutorial.title: Compare with the goal
tutorial.text: Find the required token and slot for each ring.

tutorial.title: Align two rings
tutorial.text: Rotate a ring one slot at a time until neighboring token positions align.

tutorial.title: Exchange tokens
tutorial.text: Use Exchange with next ring when alignment permits it.

tutorial.title: Place every token
tutorial.text: Continue rotations and exchanges until every identity and position matches the target.

tutorial.title: Review the route
tutorial.text: Look at the completed move count, replay the attempt or return to Attention Lab.

entries.name: NeuroWeave
entries.introduction: Plan a path through a luminous directed network while balancing energy, required targets and the exact goal of the puzzle.
entries.purpose: Explore constrained route planning and deliberate decisions using visible connection rules and energy consequences.
entries.audience: Independent readers who enjoy visual, memory and reasoning challenges.
entries.age_guidance: Choose by reading comfort and puzzle familiarity. A numeric age recommendation has not yet been published.
entries.difficulty: Typical initial networks use about 5–7, 8–12 or 13–20 nodes. Custom networks and objectives are supported; these ranges are not a fixed maximum.
entries.status: In development. Application mechanics are documented here; this is not a playable web game.
objectives: Read the objective before choosing a route.
Compare edge costs and node effects with available energy.
Use required targets, keys and challenges to plan a valid solution.
offers: Connected forward routes with clear start and destination markers.
Energy, chargers, drains, keys, barriers and challenge nodes.
Reach, shortest-route, maximum-energy and combined objectives.
Custom authored networks, evolving connections and optional hidden connections.

interaction.see: A directed network with start, destination, energy, required threshold and move count. Number labels identify nodes; they do not specify numerical visiting order.
interaction.hear: Optional effects and ambience. The rules, energy and challenges remain visible as text and graphics.
interaction.do: Follow legal connected edges, consider energy effects, collect required keys or targets and answer a node challenge when presented.
interaction.feedback: Remaining energy and moves update after actions. Memory challenges conceal the map and relevant history until answered. Challenges trigger once; recovery retains their outcomes.
interaction.progression: More nodes, node types and objectives create richer decisions. Current routes prohibit revisits. Recovery restarts the route with retained outcomes and counts as assistance.
interaction.help: Read the stated goal and energy before each move. Use How to Play, progressive hints, zoom/pan and Fit network. Pause or save before leaving.

tutorial.title: Read the full goal
tutorial.text: Check destination, required energy, intermediate targets and whether the goal is reach, shortest route, maximum energy or a combination.

tutorial.title: Inspect legal connections
tutorial.text: Start at the marked node and follow connected arrows. A smaller node number can be a valid next move; numeric order is irrelevant.

tutorial.title: Budget the next move
tutorial.text: Each edge normally costs one energy. Account for chargers, drains, keys, barriers and any required targets before committing.

tutorial.title: Handle challenges
tutorial.text: Read the displayed challenge and its consequences. For a memory question the relevant map and history are hidden until the answer is committed.

tutorial.title: Reach the objective or recover
tutorial.text: Complete the exact goal. If needed, use recovery with retained challenge outcomes; it is recorded as help rather than a new reward.

tutorial.title: Analyze and return
tutorial.text: Review the route and energy changes, replay or return to Logic Lab.

entries.name: CodeQuest
entries.introduction: Decode private numeric rows by comparing your guesses with aggregate feedback and narrowing the remaining possibilities.
entries.purpose: Practice deduction, hypothesis tracking and evidence-based elimination without revealing which individual digit produced each feedback symbol.
entries.audience: Independent readers who enjoy visual, memory and reasoning challenges.
entries.age_guidance: Choose by reading comfort and puzzle familiarity. A numeric age recommendation has not yet been published.
entries.difficulty: Easy: 1 secret row. Medium: 2. Hard: 3. Each row contains three distinct digits from 1–9. Computer opponents offer Beginner, Advanced and Expert strengths.
entries.status: In development. Application mechanics are documented here; this is not a playable web game.
objectives: Separate a correct digit from a correctly placed digit.
Compare evidence within the same row.
Revise private hypotheses without changing submitted guesses.
offers: Solo practice, three computer-opponent strengths and a local two-player duel on one device.
Editable or randomized secrets that are hidden after Confirm & Lock.
Private cell annotations with undo; public submitted guess history.
Optional 30, 60 or 120 second turn clock, off by default.

interaction.see: Private setup rows followed by public guess history and target/molecule feedback totals for each row.
interaction.hear: Optional touch effects and ambience; spoken questions and online voice interaction are not part of this game.
interaction.do: Lock valid secret rows, choose one opposing row per turn and submit three distinct digits. Use the feedback totals to revise your next guess.
interaction.feedback: A target counts a correct digit in its correct position. A molecule counts a correct digit elsewhere in that same row. Feedback is aggregate and never labels individual guessed digits.
interaction.progression: More rows increase the deduction task. In competitive modes the second player receives an equalizing final turn; optional timeouts pass the turn without a guess.
interaction.help: Use the visible history and private annotations to record hypotheses. Undo changes marks, not submitted guesses. How to Play and guided practice explain the feedback.

tutorial.title: Choose the mode
tutorial.text: Select solo practice, a computer strength or a local two-player duel, then choose the row difficulty and optional clock.

tutorial.title: Set and lock the secret
tutorial.text: Enter three different digits from 1–9 in each row, or randomize. Edit before Confirm & Lock and keep private setup hidden from the other player.

tutorial.title: Submit one row guess
tutorial.text: Choose an unsolved opposing row and submit three different digits.

tutorial.title: Interpret totals
tutorial.text: Targets indicate exact positions; molecules indicate correct digits in other positions within that row. The totals do not identify specific digits.

tutorial.title: Narrow the possibilities
tutorial.text: Compare successive row results, mark private hypotheses and undo marks when your reasoning changes.

tutorial.title: Finish fairly
tutorial.text: Solve the required rows. Local duel uses a handoff screen and an equalizing final turn; review the outcome and return to Logic Lab.

entries.name: Rule Shift
entries.introduction: Classify each symbol using the highlighted attribute, then adapt when the active rule changes.
entries.purpose: Practice attending to the current rule and setting aside a classification that no longer applies.
entries.audience: Independent readers who enjoy visual, memory and reasoning challenges.
entries.age_guidance: Choose by reading comfort and puzzle familiarity. A numeric age recommendation has not yet been published.
entries.difficulty: Easy: 2 rules over 8 items, changing every 4. Medium: 3 rules over 12 items, every 3. Hard: 4 rules over 16 items, every 2.
entries.status: In development. Application mechanics are documented here; this is not a playable web game.
objectives: Identify which attribute currently matters.
Select a category using that attribute alone.
Adjust to a rule change before the next response.
offers: Shape, color, size and fill classifications as difficulty increases.
A visible active-rule label before a choice.
A fixed, internally consistent rule schedule for each round.

interaction.see: One symbol, a highlighted active rule and its category choices.
interaction.hear: Optional interaction effects and ambience; the current rule is readable on screen.
interaction.do: Classify the symbol only by the active attribute, then check the rule again for the next item.
interaction.feedback: Each response is evaluated against the active rule and recorded as correct or an error. The following item may use a new rule.
interaction.progression: Higher difficulty adds attributes and changes the rule more frequently.
interaction.help: Treat the highlighted rule as the only classification that matters now. Use How to Play, guided practice, hints or pause.

tutorial.title: Read the active rule
tutorial.text: Check whether this response is about shape, color, size or fill.

tutorial.title: Classify the symbol
tutorial.text: Choose the matching category using only that attribute.

tutorial.title: Check again
tutorial.text: Before answering the next item, look for a changed rule rather than repeating the previous classification.

tutorial.title: Complete and review
tutorial.text: Work through the remaining items and review your recorded responses.

entries.name: Synapse Forge
entries.introduction: Investigate how a set of symbols changes, test your own inputs and use the discovered rule to transform new examples.
entries.purpose: Explore hypothesis testing and consistent rule application by comparing evidence from input/output pairs.
entries.audience: Independent readers who enjoy visual, memory and reasoning challenges.
entries.age_guidance: Choose by reading comfort and puzzle familiarity. A numeric age recommendation has not yet been published.
entries.difficulty: Easy changes 1 attribute, Medium 2 and Hard 3. Each attribute cycles through four values; response sets contain 3, 4 or 5 queries.
entries.status: In development. Application mechanics are documented here; this is not a playable web game.
objectives: Compare several input/output examples.
Test one changed attribute while holding others steady.
Apply a discovered transformation consistently to unfamiliar input.
offers: Example transformations with visible inputs and outputs.
A working Test hypothesis control for user-selected input.
Independent deduction queries using the same hidden rules.

interaction.see: Example input/output symbol groups, editable experiment input and a new deduction query.
interaction.hear: Optional touch effects and ambience; no spoken rule explanation or narration is supplied.
interaction.do: Study examples, change an experimental input and test it, then submit the transformed output for each query.
interaction.feedback: An experiment reveals the exact output from the hidden rules. Submitted deductions are scored by whether all three output attributes match.
interaction.progression: More attributes change at higher difficulty. Guided practice requires at least one real experiment before a deduction.
interaction.help: Change one attribute at a time to distinguish causes. More experiments are available; How to Play and progressive hints support reasoning.

tutorial.title: Compare examples
tutorial.text: Look for how each attribute changes from input to output.

tutorial.title: Test a hypothesis
tutorial.text: Choose your own input and select Test hypothesis. In guided practice, do this at least once before submitting a deduction.

tutorial.title: Refine one attribute
tutorial.text: Keep two attributes fixed while changing another, then compare the output with your prediction.

tutorial.title: Apply the rule
tutorial.text: Set the expected output for the new query and submit it.

tutorial.title: Continue consistently
tutorial.text: Use the same discovered transformations for the remaining queries, then review or return to Flexibility Lab.
